title: Banjo and guitar rhythm, fingers versus picks
summary: Glass explains banjo being used without piano and how guitarists played with fingers, picks or bone.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: You see, your band, when they didn't have a piano, would you use a ghetto? A banjo, you know. We'd use banjo more. Banjo. When they stomp off like that, everybody's come in. That's how we'd give our sign. So now the fellas tell you, we know this what you're going to do, in a brass band.
Did they have many guitar players that would just play with their fingers and wouldn't use a pick ever?
Bob. He played with his fingers. Had a con there.

Yeah. They'd have a con that play. Some of them fellas use that pick. Some of them would use their, they'd use a little, a little bone. They'd file that bone, a piece of waist bone. They'd file it and they'd get them strings too. Don't think they wouldn't hit them.
Could they make themselves hurt when they used them?
Oh yeah, they could hit them strings. They can get to them, in between them strings.
Yeah, but I mean when they just used their fingers would they make themselves hurt?
Yeah, loud, loud. Yeah, it's good. Well that pick would get up when they were going to put that rhythm, you know, they'd use that pick.
But for solos, what would they use?
They could pick with their fingers. Some of them pick their fingers good. Their fingers would just that hard, you know.
Yeah. Yeah, you can see them have a con on their hands.
Oh yeah. Oh yeah. And they'd hit it with that fingernail, you know. They know how to get to them.
